title: Agent Doctor
excerpt: Observe, experiment, and debug your AI agent pipelines

Your existing code. Unchanged.

Two lines to capture. One webhook handler to re-run. Agent Doctor hooks into LLM SDKs, vector databases and tool calls at the library level, so your agent logic stays exactly as-is.

support_agent.py

# Add these two lines, that's it
import agent_doctor
agent_doctor.init(api_key="sk-proj-...")

# Your existing agent logic, unchanged
# LLM calls, vector DB queries and tool calls are auto-captured

def handle_ticket(query, customer_id):
    # LLM call → auto-captured
    intent = openai.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": query}]
    )

    # Vector DB lookup → auto-captured
    docs = pinecone_index.query(vector=embed(query), top_k=5)

    # Tool call → auto-captured
    policy = check_refund_policy(customer_id)

    # LLM call → auto-captured
    response = openai.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": f"Docs: {docs} Policy: {policy}"},
                  {"role": "user", "content": query}]
    )
    return response

# Your webhook handler. payload is the run Agent Doctor sends.
def on_run(payload):
    with agent_doctor.run_context(run_id=payload.run_id, overrides=payload.overrides):
        result = handle_ticket(payload.query, payload.customer_id)
        # Every step auto-captured. Overrides auto-injected. Done.

Probe finds the broken node by asking you a few questions.

Tell it what the agent should have said and what it said instead. It walks the trace with you, asking three or four plain-English questions, and names the exact step that caused the failure. No logs, no code, no debugging skills needed.

  • A chat, so anyone on the team can run it
  • Checks the pipeline by halves, so it needs only a few questions
  • Highlights the broken node in the trace
  • Hands the fix straight to the prompt optimizer

Probe

Question 2

My agent should return a refund confirmation, but instead it's asking the customer to call support.

Got it. Let me trace through the pipeline. The router node received the customer's request and routed it to "refund_handler." Its output was:

"Customer requests refund for order #4821." Does this routing look correct?

Yes, that's right.

Good. The refund_handler then looked up order #4821 and produced:

"Order found. Status: delivered. Refund policy: eligible within 30 days." Does this look correct?

Yes, that's correct too.

Root cause found: response_composer

All upstream nodes are healthy. The response_composer node received correct refund eligibility data but generated a "call support" response instead of processing the refund.

Suggestion: The prompt lacks explicit instruction to confirm eligible refunds directly.

The optimizer writes, tests and ranks better prompts for you.

Pick a node and define what "good" looks like. The optimizer generates prompt variants, runs them against your examples, and ranks the results. It starts with GEPA, a genetic strategy that evolves prompts across generations, with more strategies on the way.

  • Evolves prompts across generations and keeps the fittest
  • Rephrases, expands, compresses and recombines winning traits
  • Ranks every variant by its score on your examples, with token cost weighed in
  • Shows the winning prompt side by side with the original prompt

Why not just use a regular observability tool?

Most LLM tracing platforms run experiments on their own cloud, so your agent can't reach your private databases, RAG, or internal tools during a test. They also keep prompt iteration locked behind code, leaving your domain experts out.

Common questions

The trace, and only the trace. Re-runs use remote-triggered execution: your webhook runs the agent inside your own infrastructure, where it already reaches your private databases, vector stores and internal tools, and Agent Doctor never connects to any of them. What it receives is the trace your SDK sends: each step's inputs, outputs and timings, which is what the dashboard shows you.

Two lines to capture: import the SDK and call

init(). It auto-instruments your LLM calls, vector DB lookups, tool executions, and API requests at the library level, with no decorators or refactors in your agent logic. To re-run from the dashboard, add one webhook handler that calls your agent inside

run_context(). After that, every prompt change is a re-run, not a redeploy.

A Python SDK today, with JavaScript/TypeScript next. It auto-instruments the libraries listed at the top of this page, from OpenAI and Anthropic to LangChain, LlamaIndex and the major vector databases.

Yes. Domain experts get a visual dashboard to inspect every step, rewrite prompts in plain English, adjust the temperature, and re-run, all without opening the codebase. Developers stay focused on building.

# Add these two lines, that's it
import agent_doctor
agent_doctor.init(api_key="sk-proj-...")

# Your existing agent logic, unchanged
# LLM calls, vector DB queries and tool calls are auto-captured

def handle_ticket(query, customer_id):
    # LLM call → auto-captured
    intent = openai.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": query}]
    )

    # Vector DB lookup → auto-captured
    docs = pinecone_index.query(vector=embed(query), top_k=5)

    # Tool call → auto-captured
    policy = check_refund_policy(customer_id)

    # LLM call → auto-captured
    response = openai.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": f"Docs: {docs} Policy: {policy}"},
                  {"role": "user", "content": query}]
    )
    return response

# Your webhook handler. payload is the run Agent Doctor sends.
def on_run(payload):
    with agent_doctor.run_context(run_id=payload.run_id, overrides=payload.overrides):
        result = handle_ticket(payload.query, payload.customer_id)
        # Every step auto-captured. Overrides auto-injected. Done.
